summary: Full backend + frontend test of the new Springfield, X town feature. Backend: 17 pytest cases (test_town_backend.py) — all critical endpoints pass (town shape+unchanged diff, finished/reserved residents, 404 unknown, card.jpg JPEG 3:4 for finished + 404 for reserved, share page HTML with og/twitter cards for bots and 302 for browsers, move-in happy/already/invalid/not_found/lights_on, admin check without/with key, hide/restore roundtrip including town removal + resident 404 + move-in 403). Frontend: town map renders with houses, landmarks, Town Hall, stat stickers, ticker, move-in bar, fan disclaimer; finished house click opens resident-sheet (title, tier, neighbourhood, brought, neighbours×8, share, x-link); clicking a neighbour switches the sheet; search opens with search-input, prefix shows search-result-{k} + search-move-in-button for unknown; reserved sheet shows resident-move-in-button; arrival sheet at /h/levelsio?arrive=1 shows title '@levelsio's street', 3 arrival-tagged-* buttons, tapping one opens the reserved resident-sheet with MOVE IN; /h/<unknown> shows '@x isn\'t in town yet.' with move-in button; move-in with a non-existent handle shows move-in-progress then move-in-error 'There's no X account called @...'; Town Hall landmark navigates to /timeline which still renders 24 prediction cards and back-to-town-link; owner mode via /?admin=KEY strips the param and exposes resident-hide-button on sheets. Mobile 390x844: zero horizontal overflow; header, search, ticker, move-in bar and sheet all fit the viewport.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 651 lines — approaching the 700-line soft cap; consider splitting the move-in job runner, admin, share-page and card routes into separate modules for maintainability.

CORS is configured with allow_credentials=True while allow_origins defaults to '*' (via CORS_ORIGINS env). Browsers reject credentials with wildcard origins; set explicit origins in prod to avoid surprises.

GET /api/town returns the full residents array on every version change — fine for current scale (~45 residents) but will grow linearly. Consider ETag/If-None-Match or delta diffs when the town grows past a few hundred residents.
fetch_avatar() silently clears AVATAR_CACHE at 600 entries (hard cutover). Prefer an LRU to avoid cold-start thrash when many cards are rendered in parallel.
move-in error code 'failed' is a generic bucket — UI maps every non-'not_found' error to a single toast. Surfacing 'blocked' / 'rate-limited' / 'read_failed' separately in the UI would help users.
Ticker events use key 'h' (handle) only; adding a canonical 'k' (lowercased key) in the event payload would make client-side matching robust against case changes.
